system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: SPIRE-2 NCT01975389 - The Evaluation of Bococizumab (PF-04950615; RN316) in Reducing the Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular Events in High Risk Subjects
Investigational drug: bococizumab
Document: A Mechanism-Based Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Model for Bococizumab, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Against Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type 9, and Its Application in Early Clinical Development. (journal, published 2017-02-09, source pmid:28181260)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
A Mechanism-Based Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Model for Bococizumab, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Against Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type 9, and Its Application in Early Clinical Development.

Bococizumab (RN316/PF-04950615), a humanized monoclonal antibody, binds to secreted proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) and prevents its downregulation of low-density lipoprotein receptor, leading to improved clearance and reduction of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in plasma. A mechanism-based drug-target binding model was developed, accounting for bococizumab, PCSK9, and LDL-C concentrations and the effects of concomitant administration of statins. This model was utilized to better understand the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) data obtained from 3 phase 1 and 2 phase 2a clinical studies. First, simulations performed with this model demonstrated that the conventional method of the area-under-the-curve ratio for bioavailability determination underestimated the subcutaneous bioavailability of bococizumab due to its target-mediated disposition. Second, a covariate model component for statin effects on bococizumab PK/PD was characterized, including a description of the decreased baseline LDL-C, increased baseline PCSK9, and increased LDL-C lowering with concomitant use of statins. Last, the impact of the dosing regimens with and without a dose holiday on bococizumab's LDL-C-lowering effectiveness was shown to be predictable due to the well-characterized PK-PD relationship.
--- END ---
